description: Add real, tenant-scoped backend endpoints on the collections controller to back the driver assignment/release/workflow flows that the Collections command center calls. Currently the frontend calls collection-ops/* and collections-state-sync/auto-assign|release|workflow routes that DO NOT EXIST, and POST /drivers/assign / POST /collections/:id/assign-driver do not exist either. The Collection Prisma model already has driverId (String?) and status (CollectionStatus incl. ASSIGNED), so assign/release map cleanly onto existing fields with NO schema changes. Add: (a) POST /collections/:id/assign-driver, (b) POST /collections/:id/release-driver, (c) GET /collections/:id/workflow (a read model that returns the collection plus its linked driver/shipment status so the frontend drawer can render). Reuse the existing GET /drivers?status=AVAILABLE for the available-driver list (no new availability endpoint needed).
steps: In backend/src/collections/collections.service.ts add async assignDriver(id, companyId, driverId): call this.findOne(id, companyId) as the tenant ownership guard (throws NotFound if not this company's collection). Validate the driver belongs to the same company via this.prisma.driver.findFirst({ where: { id: driverId, companyId } }) and throw NotFoundException('Driver not found') if missing. Then this.prisma.collection.update({ where: { id }, data: { driverId, status: 'ASSIGNED' } }) and return the updated collection including { driver: true }. Follow the existing service style (see update() and confirmCollected()).

In collections.service.ts add async releaseDriver(id, companyId): call this.findOne(id, companyId) guard, then prisma.collection.update({ where: { id }, data: { driverId: null, status: 'PENDING' } }) and return the updated collection. Only reset status to PENDING when it is currently ASSIGNED (leave IN_PROGRESS/COLLECTED/etc untouched to avoid clobbering downstream state) — read the current status from the findOne result and branch accordingly.

In collections.service.ts add async getWorkflow(id, companyId): call findOne(id, companyId) (includes driver + agent), then assemble a read model the drawer expects. Return an object shaped like { collection: { id, reference: collection.id, customerName: clientName, destination: pickupAddress, syncHealth, aiPriority, driverName, driverId }, driver: collection.driver ? { id, name, vehicleType } : null, dispatch: null, shipment: null, pod: null, invoice: null, nextActions: [] }. Derive driverName from collection.driver?.name. Keep it defensive: the frontend already tolerates missing/undefined sub-objects (resolveCollectionTruth uses optional chaining), so returning a minimal-but-consistent object is sufficient. Do NOT invent Prisma relations that don't exist — only Collection.driver exists on the model.

In backend/src/collections/collections.controller.ts add the three routes following the file's existing style (each decorator carries the full path, @CurrentUser() u: any, u.companyId): @Post('collections/:id/assign-driver') assignDriver(@Param('id') id, @CurrentUser() u, @Body() body: { driverId: string }) => svc.assignDriver(id, u.companyId, body.driverId); @Post('collections/:id/release-driver') releaseDriver(@Param('id') id, @CurrentUser() u) => svc.releaseDriver(id, u.companyId); @Get('collections/:id/workflow') workflow(@Param('id') id, @CurrentUser() u) => svc.getWorkflow(id, u.companyId). Place :id/workflow and the POST sub-routes AFTER the existing @Get('collections/:id') is fine because they have distinct suffixes; keep them grouped near confirm-collected/auto-suggest for readability.

Do NOT modify prisma/schema.prisma — no new fields or models are required. Do NOT create a collection-ops controller or a collections-state-sync/auto-assign route; the assignment lives on the collections resource which is the correct owner of the Collection.driverId field.

Confirm the DriversController GET /drivers already forwards ?status to prisma (drivers.service.ts findAll applies where.status = query.status). No backend change needed for availability; FEAT-002 will point the frontend at GET /drivers?status=AVAILABLE.
acceptance_criteria: backend/src/collections/collections.controller.ts declares POST collections/:id/assign-driver, POST collections/:id/release-driver, and GET collections/:id/workflow, each using @CurrentUser() u and passing u.companyId to the service.
collections.service.ts assignDriver validates driver ownership by companyId and sets Collection.driverId + status ASSIGNED; releaseDriver clears driverId and only resets ASSIGNED->PENDING.
No changes to prisma/schema.prisma (git diff shows schema.prisma unchanged).
New service methods reuse this.findOne(id, companyId) as the tenant guard, matching existing collections.service.ts methods.
verification: Read collections.controller.ts and confirm the three new routes exist and are company-scoped via @CurrentUser().

Read collections.service.ts and confirm assignDriver/releaseDriver/getWorkflow use PrismaService + findOne guard and reference only existing Collection fields (driverId, status) and the Collection.driver relation.
Run `git -C /projects/sandbox/Flowops diff --stat backend/prisma/schema.prisma` and confirm zero changes to the schema.
Static TypeScript sanity: confirm no references to non-existent Prisma relations/fields were introduced (grep the new methods).
findings: Implemented on collections resource only (no collection-ops/collections-state-sync additions). Added service methods assignDriver/releaseDriver/getWorkflow to collections.service.ts and routes POST collections/:id/assign-driver, POST collections/:id/release-driver, GET collections/:id/workflow to collections.controller.ts, grouped after auto-suggest. All tenant-scoped via this.findOne(id, companyId) guard + @CurrentUser() u.companyId, matching existing style. assignDriver validates driver ownership with prisma.driver.findFirst({ id, companyId }) and throws NotFoundException('Driver not found'). releaseDriver clears driverId and only resets status ASSIGNED->PENDING (reads current status from findOne result). getWorkflow returns the minimal read model shape from step 3, referencing only Collection.driver (verified in schema.prisma lines 519+ / 1123+: Collection has driverId/status/clientName/pickupAddress + driver relation; Driver has name String, vehicleType String). Verified backend/prisma/schema.prisma has ZERO diff. status assignment uses data:any object, consistent with existing update(). Could NOT run nest build/tsc: no node/npm runtime in sandbox per context.json (owner builds via Docker on VPS). Verification was static: confirmed field/relation existence against schema.prisma and grepped new methods for non-existent relations (none found; dispatch/pod/invoice are literal null keys, not Prisma accesses). Working on non-default branch feat/api-health-monitor; committed there per branch policy.
